questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: The determinant of a three by three matrix
questions.stem: Lab record 58: a clerk expands a 3x3 determinant and uses all plus signs, no minuses.

options.text: The clerk is right; all terms are added.
options.misconception: names "The clerk is right; all terms are added" where the rule requires "The clerk is wrong; cofactor signs must alternate"

options.text: Only the first term needs a minus.
Signs do not matter for determinants.
The clerk is wrong; cofactor signs must alternate.

questions.explanation: Cofactor expansion requires alternating signs according to the checkerboard pattern. All plus signs give a wrong determinant.

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.stem: Lab record 59: explain what it means for a matrix to be singular.

answer.exemplar: A singular matrix has determinant zero, so it is not invertible; its columns are linearly dependent and the associated system may lack a unique solution.

questions.explanation: The invertibility and the determinant principle here is: Zero determinant. On that basis "A singular matrix has determinant zero, so it is not invertible; its columns are linearly dependent and the associated system may lack a unique solution" is correct.

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: A system written as a matrix equation
questions.stem: Lab record 60: in Ax=b, what do the columns of A represent?

options.text: Coefficients of the variables in each equation.
The constants on the right-hand side.
options.misconception: names "The constants on the right-hand side" where the rule requires "Coefficients of the variables in each equation"

questions.explanation: The rule that settles this a system written as a matrix equation item is: Coefficients, not constants. That is why "Coefficients of the variables in each equation" is right. The option "The solutions of the system" (confuses inputs with outputs) does not satisfy the rule.
